description:
Evaluate candidate architectures for the v2 replay engine and pick one. DECIDED 2026-05-13.

PRIMARY: persistent native Rust sidecar helper process. Electron launches it on app start, communicates over length-prefixed JSON-RPC on a UNIX domain socket (Linux/macOS) or named pipe (Windows). The sidecar owns capture (PipeWire on Linux, WGC on Windows later), encoder backends (NVENC / VAAPI / QSV / AMF / libx264 via libavcodec through the ffmpeg-next crate), rolling segment ring buffer, and export/remux. Electron is UI + control plane only.

FALLBACK: ffmpeg-driven helper process with PipeWire input. Same sidecar shape, same IPC contract, but the inner engine is a managed ffmpeg child process. Same encoder coverage, brittle CLI driving, kept as the escape hatch and Linux-first viability check.

REJECTED: on-demand native binary launched per command (cannot hold continuous rolling replay buffer); Node N-API addon (per-Electron-version ABI coupling, per-platform prebuild matrix, crash takes UI down — hostile to solo maintenance).

OUTPUT: decision recorded in .story/notes/N-002.json and .story/project-state.md under 'v2.0.0 replay engine decision'. No source file changes.

DOWNSTREAM: T-004 designs the PipeWire CaptureSource. T-005 designs the EncoderBackend matrix and probe order. T-006 designs the rolling segment ring buffer. T-007 designs the export/remux pipeline. T-008 designs the Electron-engine IPC contract.

HARD CONSTRAINT REAFFIRMED: do not continue patching the v1 MediaRecorder pipeline as the long-term v2 solution.
title: Research and choose native replay engine approach
